_note: Context presets. A preset sets the proof standard of the claim and whether sources are required, and may weigh the schemes as an audience in that context would (Carneades reads an argument's weight as the audience's assessment of it). The weights below are DRAFTS for discussion, not values from Walton or the CAF: change them, or play 'equal' to let the structure alone decide.

contexts.name: Everyday discussion
contexts.description: An informal exchange, as on Kialo: the side with the stronger case wins (preponderance of the evidence). Sources are optional. The schemes keep their default weights.

contexts.name: Policy question
contexts.description: What should be done, argued pro and con: arguments from goals, values and consequences carry the most weight; the stronger case wins. The game is still a persuasion dialogue about a practical claim, not a deliberation (docs/dialogue-types.md).

contexts.name: Scientific question
contexts.description: What is true, argued pro and con: evidence and expertise carry the most weight, goals and values the least; the claim must be clear and convincing, and sources are required. The game is still an adversarial persuasion dialogue, not a cooperative inquiry (docs/dialogue-types.md).

contexts.name: Legal case (criminal)
contexts.description: Guilt beyond reasonable doubt: witnesses, experts, circumstantial signs and precedent carry the most weight; sources are required. A moderator plays the judge.

contexts.name: Equal weights
contexts.description: Every scheme weighs 0.5, so only the structure of the dispute (which premises hold, which exceptions are argued) decides. For testing the rules.
